transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too, Doc. Well, I came in because... I keep steering clear of my own workshop. And any family get-together where my brother-in-law might show up, I avoid those too. I guess, after all this time, I'm just tired of planning my whole life around not running into those reminders. I figured it was time to finally talk to somebody about it.
Did something traumatic happen in your workshop or involving your brother-in-law?
Yeah, it was both, actually. We had a... well, a confrontation out in the workshop. This whole thing has been going on ever since that happened, which was about two years and four months ago now.
Do memories of that confrontation ever come back into your mind when you don't want them to?

Yeah, they do. Out of nowhere, really. I'll just be standing there, maybe shaving or... or working on one of my paintings, and suddenly I see his hand holding that heavy tool again. It's like a picture that just pops right into my head. Even after all this time, it still makes my chest tighten up when it happens.
Do you have nightmares about what happened in the workshop?

Yeah, I do. Most nights I can get to bed okay, but... well, I just lie there listening for noises in the house. Or I'll wake up from a bad dream about the workshop. And once that happens, I'm usually wide awake for an hour or two before I can settle back down.
Since that confrontation, do you feel constantly on guard, like you're watching for danger even when you're safe?

Yeah, I do. Even when I'm somewhere completely safe, like at the senior center or down in the church basement, I find myself checking who just came in. I always make sure I know exactly where the door is... and I'm constantly checking whether anyone is standing too close behind me. I just can't seem to drop my guard.
When something reminds you of that confrontation, do you suddenly feel very upset?

No, I wouldn't really say I get very upset. I mean, like I mentioned before, my chest might get a little tight if the memory just pops into my head, but... I don't get all emotional or break down if I see something that reminds me of it. I just kind of brush it off and keep doing whatever I'm doing.
During that confrontation in the workshop, did you believe that you might be seriously injured or killed?

No, I didn't think he was going to kill me or anything like that. I mean, it was tense, and he was really in my face yelling, but... I didn't think I was in any real physical danger of being seriously hurt. It was just a very ugly situation.
During that confrontation, did your brother-in-law threaten to seriously hurt you?

No, he didn't. I mean, he was shouting and saying a lot of nasty things, but... he never actually said he was going to hit me or put me in the hospital or anything. It was just a lot of loud, angry talk, no actual threats like that.
When you avoid family gatherings where your brother-in-law might be there, is it because you’re afraid other people will judge or embarrass you?

No, it's not that. I'm not worried about being embarrassed or what other people might think of me. At my age, I don't really care much about that sort of thing. It's just... I'd rather avoid the headache of being around him, you know? It doesn't have anything to do with the rest of the family judging me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I have my moments, but... I don't feel down or depressed most days. I get up, do what I need to do around the house. It's not like a dark cloud hanging over me all the time or anything.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things in your life, even when they have nothing to do with your brother-in-law or the workshop?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things now and then, like the bills or the car needing work, but... I don't sit around worrying all day about everything under the sun. It's just the usual stuff, nothing out of the ordinary.
When you think about going into your workshop or being somewhere your brother-in-law might be, do you feel afraid?

Afraid? No, I wouldn't use that word. I mean, I'm not scared of my brother-in-law, and I'm certainly not scared of my own workshop. It's just... I just really don't want to be around him or in that space. Like I said before, it's more about avoiding the whole headache of it all. So no, I don't feel afraid.
